x.ASV: Oh that my head were waters, and mine eyes a fountain of tears, that I might weep day and night for the slain of the daughter of my people!
x.Darby: Oh that my head were waters, and mine eye a fountain of tears, that I might weep day and night for the slain of the daughter of my people!
x.KJV: Oh that my head were waters, and mine eyes a fountain of tears, that I might weep day and night for the slain of the daughter of my people!

nt: Here Jeremiah wishes his head were **waters** and his eyes were **a fountain of tears**. He means that he wants to weep continually for his people. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I could produce tears without ceasing]

Jeremiah is referring to all of the time by naming two major components, **day** and **night**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [continually]

Jeremiah is using the adjective **slain** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [for the people who have been killed among]

Here Jeremiah is speaking of his fellow Israelites as if they were a **daughter**. He uses this expression to speak of his people tenderly, as a father would speak of his own child. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [my people, whom I love as my own child]

x.ASV: Oh that I had in the wilderness a lodging-place of wayfaring men; that I might leave my people, and go from them! for they are all adulterers, an assembly of treacherous men.

x.KJV: Oh that I had in the wilderness a lodging place of wayfaring men; that I might leave my people, and go from them! for they be all adulterers, an assembly of treacherous men.

nt: Jeremiah is using the question form to express a wish. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [I wish someone would give me a lodging place of travelers in the desert, that I might leave my people and walk away from them!]

Here Jeremiah is speaking of his people as if they were **adulterers**. He means that they have been unfaithful to Yahweh. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [For all of them are unfaithful to Yahweh]

Jeremiah is saying **all of them are adulterers** as a generalization for emphasis. If it would be clearer in your language, you could express the emphasis in a different way. Alternate translation: [almost all of them are adulterers]

nt: Here Yahweh is speaking as if the people’s tongues were **their bow**, which they bend by treading on it in order to shoot lies. Yahweh is using **from evil thing to evil thing they go** as a common expression of the culture to mean “they commit one wicked act after another.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [For they proceed from one wicked act to another]

Jeremiah is using **the declaration of Yahweh** to indicate that what has been said is a direct quotation from Yahweh and comes with Yahweh’s authority. In your translation, use a natural way of indicating direct quotations in your language.

Alternate translation: [Each one of you must beware of your neighbor]

Yahweh is repeating forms of the verb **deceives** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. Here Yahweh is speaking of habitual behavior as if it were the way a person **walks**. He means that every neighbor regularly slanders others. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and every neighbor habitually slanders others]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **deceit**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [among people who act deceitfully; because they are deceitful]

Yahweh is using **Behold me** as an expression that people of this culture would commonly use to mean that they were about to do something. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Now I am about to refine them]

If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Yahweh is using **he speaks peace** as a common expression of the culture to mean “he greets someone in a friendly way.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Yahweh is using **in his midst** as a common expression of the culture to mean “inwardly.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Here Yahweh is speaking of secretly planning to harm someone as if a person were setting an **ambush** for him. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [he secretly plans to harm him]

Jeremiah is using **take up weeping and wailing** as a common expression of the culture to mean “begin to mourn loudly.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. The word translated as **Because** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. nt: The expression **is heard** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [people hear the sound of wailing from Zion]

If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [from Zion, that they are devastated]

The people of Jerusalem are using a phrase that expresses a strong feeling of grief and dismay. There may be an equivalent word or phrase in your language that you can use in your translation to convey this feeling. Alternate translation: [We are utterly devastated!]

The point of this comparison is that just as **dung** lies scattered on a field and no one gathers it, so will the bodies of the dead lie on the ground with no one to bury them. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [and the corpse of man will lie unburied and disregarded like dung]

Yahweh is not referring to a specific **corpse**. He means the bodies of dead people in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the dead bodies of people]

Yahweh is using **the face of the field** as a common expression of the culture to mean “the open ground.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [upon the open ground]

The point of this comparison is that just as **sheaves** lie on the ground behind a harvester when no one collects them, so will the bodies of the dead lie there with no one to bury them. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [and lying uncollected as cut grain lies behind a harvester]
